q: Which youth football leagues play at Lasselle Sports Park?
a: Moreno Valley Pop Warner Football & Cheer was the park's first league (2014); Moreno Valley Junior All American Football (Falcons), the City's PCS Flag Football league, and NFL FLAG Inland Empire all run games or practices here — NFL FLAG practices Mon/Wed 5-7pm with Friday-night games.

q: What are the football fields like?
a: Three regulation-size natural-turf fields with field lighting, LED scoreboards, and protective netting between the fields and Lasselle Street / the Perris Valley storm drain. The fields sit on top of a state aqueduct easement.

q: Is there a concession stand or snack bar?
a: Yes — a 2,000 sq ft building houses two restrooms, storage, and a concession stand with food-prep space. The City contracts out periodic deep cleaning of the snack bar.

q: Do the fields have to be reserved, and is parking big enough?
a: Reservations go through the City Parks & Community Services reservation system; the parking lot holds roughly 200 spaces and fills quickly on weekend game days — overflow often uses the surrounding neighborhood.

q: Are there playgrounds and a walking path?
a: Two age-segregated playgrounds (ages 2-5 and 5-12, with a 12-foot climbing structure), plus picnic shelters and BBQ grills. A decomposed-granite loop around the fields serves as a ~0.4-mile walking/running path with outdoor fitness equipment.

q: What is the history of the park?
a: Originally promised in 1990 as part of the Moreno Valley Ranch subdivision. After three developers went bankrupt, the city's bonding company built the $6.5 million park at no cost to the city; construction began Sept 2012 and the park dedicated Sept 27, 2014.
Daily, 6:00 AM to 10:00 PM (Park phone: 951-413-3000; Parks & Community Services Dept: 951-413-3280).
